source.title: Improving Diffusion Generalization with Weak-to-Strong Segmented Guidance
source.authors: Liangyu Yuan; Yufei Huang; Mingkun Lei; Tong Zhao; Ruoyu Wang; Changxi Chi; Yiwei Wang; Chi Zhang

record.tranche_reason: Extends the weak-to-strong idea to continuous diffusion generation in image and video settings, including training-time changes, but uses guidance signals and a modified velocity target rather than fine-tuning on labels produced by a weaker model.
record.gate_note: The paper does not measure Burns et al.'s PGR, compare a student against the weak supervisor, or use weak-model-produced labels. It reports diffusion generation metrics for training variants that incorporate weak-to-strong guidance; these are recorded for V6 as evidence about applying a related effect outside language. Toy-experiment descriptions and inference-time comparisons are not included as rows because they do not test the training-time modality effect captured here.
record.test_reason: The paper borrows the 'weak-to-strong' label for diffusion guidance, but this is a different construct from Burns et al.'s weak-to-strong generalization. A weaker signal (unconditional output, smaller SiT-S/2, or a shallow branch) is used as a direction to extrapolate away from. The strong model still trains on ground-truth flow-matching targets. No strong model is trained on a weak supervisor's labels. Neither the weak model's own generation quality nor PGR is reported, so nothing shows a student beating its supervisor. Burns et al. is not cited. The training-time results compare against a standard-training baseline, which makes them a training-objective improvement rather than evidence for any version, including V6.
record.authors_conclusion: Broadly correct. The authors frame CFG- and AutoGuidance-style guidance as a 'weak-to-strong principle'. They propose segmented guidance (CFG at high noise, condition-agnostic guidance at low noise) and report gains at inference on SD3/SD3.5 and Wan video. Moving this guidance into the training target improves unguided SiT-B/2 FID in conditional and unconditional ImageNet settings. They note extra training compute (e.g. 22% for SGG) and that the method is limited to continuous diffusion.
record.recipe_differences: This is diffusion velocity-field guidance and target modification, not fine-tuning a pretrained strong model on labels generated by a weaker model. No PGR is computed and weak-supervisor task performance is not compared.
record.method_sensitivity: Training results vary with W2S method and guidance scale; the SGG training configuration uses a segmented timestamp τ = 0.2. The paper also reports that training-time SLG can degrade results without warm-up.

fits_no_version.finding: On SiT-B/2 ImageNet 256, adding a guidance term to the training target lowers unguided FID versus standard training. The term extrapolates away from a weaker signal: unconditional output, smaller SiT-S/2, or shallow branch.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Training diffusion models toward targets extrapolated away from a weaker model's predictions improves unguided sample quality. This is 'weak-to-strong guidance', distinct from weak-label supervision.

record.problems: The evidence is from ImageNet diffusion experiments and uses FID, sFID, and Inception Score rather than weak-supervisor comparisons or PGR. The authors state that their approach is limited to continuous diffusion. No uncertainty estimates are reported in the cited results.
record.rows_left_out: Inference-time comparisons on SD3/SD3.5 and Wan, plus 2D toy guidance examples, were not extracted because they concern inference-time guidance or synthetic guidance regimes rather than the training-time modality effect recorded for V6.

untested.parts: No weak-label fine-tuning, no weak-supervisor performance, no PGR.
No PGR comparison of training changes against naive weak-label fine-tuning.
No variation of PGR with supervisor/student size, task, or representations.
No exploitation, distribution-shift or correlated-error tests.
No theory of when a student must beat its supervisor.
Vision setting, but no student trained on weak-model labels and no comparison to the weak model's performance; the effect itself is not measured.

record.verdict_notes: The reader's V6 'tested' and 'supports' labels are withdrawn: the shared name 'weak-to-strong' does not make this the same phenomenon. Guidance extrapolates away from weak predictions, whereas Burns-style W2S learns from weak labels, and no supervisor-vs-student comparison exists. Table 2 in the text has the AG sFID and IS columns swapped; the record already reads them correctly.

versions.untested_parts: No weak-label fine-tuning, weak-supervisor performance comparison, or PGR measurement.
Does not measure PGR or compare training changes by PGR against naive fine-tuning.
Does not test PGR variation by supervisor/student size, NLP/chess/reward-modelling task, or representations.
Does not test the stated student exploitation, distribution-shift, or correlated-error failure modes.
Does not establish theoretical conditions under which a student must beat its supervisor.

Tests related weak-to-strong guidance in continuous diffusion image generation, but not weak-label fine-tuning or PGR; it does not establish the effect for other non-language modalities such as discrete diffusion.
